items.prompt: An elephant is ___ than a cat.

options.why: We are comparing two animals, so big needs an ending.
Biggest compares three or more. Here there are only two.
We do not say more big. Short words take -er.

hints: How many animals are being compared?
Use -er to compare two things and -est for three or more.
Look for the word than. It tells you two things are being compared.
items.explanation: We are comparing two animals, so we add -er. Big doubles its g: bigger.

items.prompt: Which word compares three or more things?

options.why: Taller compares two things.
Tall describes one thing. It does not compare.
Tallness names how tall something is. It does not compare.

hints: There are two comparing endings: -er and -est.
The -er ending is for two things.
Think of a race with five children. Who won? The fast...?
items.explanation: The -est ending compares three or more things, so tallest is the word for the tallest in a group.

items.prompt:
Add -er to nice.
Your drawing is ___ than mine!
hints: You are comparing two drawings.
Nice already ends in e.
Words like nice and wide end in e. How do you add -er so there is only one e?
items.explanation: Nice ends in e, so we only add r. Nice becomes nicer.

items.prompt:
Add -est to hot.
Today is the ___ day of the week.
hints: Hot is a short word with one vowel.
Short words like hot, big and sad double their last letter.
Think of big and biggest. Do the same thing to hot.
items.explanation: Hot has one short vowel and ends in one consonant, so we double the t. Hot becomes hottest.

items.prompt: Match each word to its -er form.
hints: Look at how each word ends.
Some words double the last letter. Some change y to i. Some just add -r or -er.
Start with fast. Does it need any change before -er?
items.explanation: Fast just adds -er. Big doubles the g, wide adds -r, and happy and funny change y to i.

items.prompt: Which -er word is spelt correctly?

options.why: Busy ends in a consonant and y, so the y must change to i.
Busy has only one s.
The y changes to i. We do not keep both.

hints: Busy ends in s and then y.
When a word ends in a consonant and y, change the y to i.
Think of happy and happier. Busy follows the same rule.
items.explanation: Busy ends in a consonant and y, so the y changes to i before -er. Busy becomes busier.

items.prompt: Sort the words by how you add -er.
hints: Look at the last letters of each word.
A short word with one vowel and one last consonant doubles it. A consonant and y changes to i.
Start with thin. It has one short vowel and ends in n.
items.explanation: Thin, sad and wet double the last letter: thinner, sadder, wetter. Early, heavy and sunny change y to i. Long, quick and small just add -er.

items.prompt: Lina's bag is heavy. Omar's bag is heavier. Ben's bag is the heaviest. Whose bag is the lightest?

options.why: Omar's bag is heavier than Lina's, so it is not the lightest.
Ben's bag is the heaviest. That is the opposite!
The words heavier and heaviest show the bags are different.

hints: Find who has the heaviest bag first.
Heavier means more heavy than another bag.
Put the three bags in order from heaviest to least heavy.
items.explanation: Ben's bag is the heaviest, and Omar's is heavier than Lina's. So Lina's bag is the lightest.

items.prompt:
Use the word early.
Of all the children, Made is always the ___ to arrive at school.
hints: Made is compared with all the children, so it is more than two.
Use -est for three or more.
Early ends in a consonant and y. What happens to the y?
items.explanation: We compare Made with all the children, so we use -est. Early changes y to i: earliest.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: My kite flew highest than yours.
options.why: Use -er with than when you compare two things.

options.text: My kite flew higher than yours.
My kite flew more higher than yours.
options.why: Do not use more and -er together.

options.text: My kite flew high than yours.
options.why: High needs -er when it is used with than.

hints: How many kites are being compared?
The word than tells you two things are being compared.
Read each sentence aloud. Which one sounds like a sentence from a book?
items.explanation: We compare two kites, so we use higher. We never put more in front of an -er word.

items.prompt: This is the ___ mango I have ever eaten!

options.why: Sweet has two e letters, so we do not double the t.
Sweeter compares two things. Ever eaten means all the mangoes you have had.
Do not use most and -est together.

hints: Ever eaten means compared with all the mangoes you have had.
More than two things need the -est ending.
Sweet has a long vowel sound. Does it double the last letter?
items.explanation: The mango is compared with every mango ever eaten, so we need -est. Sweet just adds -est: sweetest.

items.prompt: The red pencil is longer than the blue pencil. The green pencil is shorter than the blue pencil. Which pencil is the longest?

options.why: The red pencil is longer than the blue one.
The green pencil is shorter than the blue one, so it is the shortest.

options.text: They are all the same length.
options.why: Longer and shorter show the pencils are different lengths.

hints: Read each clue slowly, one at a time.
Compare each pencil with the blue pencil.
Draw three lines for the pencils. Start with the blue one in the middle.
items.explanation: Red is longer than blue, and green is shorter than blue. From longest to shortest, the order is red, blue, green.

items.prompt: A mouse is ___ than an elephant.
hints: You are comparing two animals.
When we compare two things we add -er.
Which word ends in -er?
items.explanation: Smaller compares two animals. Use -er for two and -est for three or more.

items.prompt: A mouse is small. An ant is ___.
hints: We are comparing two animals.
Add er to the word.
Small plus er.
items.explanation: Smaller compares two things.

options.why: Smallest compares three or more.
We do not say more small.
Smalling is not a word.

items.prompt: The giraffe is the ___ animal.
hints: The sentence says the.
We compare it with all other animals.
Add est.
items.explanation: Tallest compares more than two.

options.why: Taller compares two.
Tall does not compare.
We do not say more tall.

items.prompt: big, bigger, ___
hints: The list goes big, bigger, then the most.
Add est.
Double the g.
items.explanation: Big, bigger, biggest.

options.why: The g needs to be doubled.
Bigger is the second word.
We do not say most big.

items.prompt: Add -er to hot. Which word is spelt right?
hints: Hot has one vowel and one end letter.
Double the t.
Then add er.
items.explanation: Hot plus er makes hotter.

options.why: The t needs to be doubled.
The ending is er.
There is an extra r.

items.prompt: Add -est to happy. Which word is spelt right?
hints: Happy ends in y.
Change y to i.
Then add est.
items.explanation: Happy becomes happiest.

options.why: Change the y to i first.
The letter i is missing.
There is an extra y.

items.prompt: Write the word. fast, faster, ___
hints: The list gets bigger each time.
Add est.
Fast plus est.
items.explanation: Fast, faster, fastest.

items.prompt: Write the word with -er. This bag is ___ than that one. (heavy)
hints: Change the y to i.
Then add er.
The word has seven letters.
items.explanation: Heavy becomes heavier.

items.prompt: Sort the words by what they compare.
hints: Look at the ending.
er is for two things.
est is for the most.
items.explanation: Taller, faster and smaller compare two. Tallest, fastest and smallest compare more.

items.prompt: Match each word to its est form.
hints: Add est to each word.
Some words change a letter.
Happy changes y to i.
items.explanation: Each word has an est form.

items.prompt: Ravi is ___ than his sister.
hints: There are two people.
The sentence has than.
Add er.
items.explanation: Taller compares two people.

items.prompt: This is the ___ day of the year.
hints: The sentence says the.
It compares with all other days.
Double the t and add est.
items.explanation: Hottest compares with all other days.

items.prompt: Which sentence is right?
hints: The class has many children.
Use the word for the most.
It ends with est.
items.explanation: Fastest compares Mia with everyone in the class.

options.text: Mia is the faster runner in the class.
options.why: Faster compares two.

options.text: Mia is the fastest runner in the class.
Mia is the most fast runner in the class.
options.why: We say fastest, not most fast.
We use faster with than.

items.prompt: What is the comparing word for good: good, ___, best?
hints: This word does not follow the er rule.
Say it with than.
The word has six letters.
items.explanation: Good, better, best is an irregular pattern.

options.why: Good is an irregular word.
We do not say more good.
Well is a different word.
